strengths: Novel and well-motivated combination of joint image+geometry generation via warping-and-inpainting, addressing both extrapolation (via diffusion) and pose-free settings (via off-the-shelf geometry predictors), which prior methods handle only separately.

The cross-modal attention instillation idea (transferring image U-Net attention maps to the geometry U-Net) is a clean and interesting mechanism, backed by an intuitive analysis (Fig. 3) of why image inpainting and geometry completion behave differently.
Proximity-based mesh conditioning and camera-space pointmap normalization are practical, well-justified engineering contributions that are shown via ablation to meaningfully improve results.

Fairly extensive empirical evaluation across three datasets (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) and multiple settings (1-view, 2-view, interpolative/extrapolative), with comparisons to a reasonably broad set of feedforward baselines (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat, DUSt3R, LVSM) and warping-and-inpainting baselines (LucidDreamer, GenWarp).

Ablation studies (component-wise and qualitative) support the individual contribution of each proposed module, and the analysis on scaling to more input views (despite training on 2 views) is a nice demonstration of flexibility.
Method directly outputs aligned geometry without requiring per-scene optimization (NeRF/3DGS), which is a practically useful property.
weaknesses: Table 5 (Depth prediction accuracy) is explicitly labeled 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled,' indicating an unfinished experiment was left in the submitted manuscript — a significant polish/rigor concern for a top-tier submission.

The paper extensively discusses generative pose-embedded NVS methods (Zero-123, MVDream, CAT3D, SV3D, ReconFusion) in related work as key competitors but never quantitatively compares against any of them, only against feedforward reconstruction methods and other warping-and-inpainting approaches; this leaves the central claimed advantage over generative NVS methods unverified.

Both the pseudo-ground-truth geometry used for training/supervision and the correspondence conditioning at inference rely on the same off-the-shelf model (VGGT), which is also used to generate conditioning for baseline warping-and-inpainting methods (LucidDreamer, GenWarp) in comparisons; this raises questions about whether reported gains stem from the proposed architecture or from favorable/matched geometry sourcing, and there is no ablation with a different geometry predictor to test robustness.

Reconstruction-style metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) used for extrapolative view synthesis are somewhat ill-suited for generative completion, since there can be multiple plausible completions for unobserved regions; no perceptual/human study or diversity metric is reported to complement pixel-wise metrics in these inherently ambiguous regions.

No analysis of computational cost, inference time, or memory footprint despite the architecture involving two full diffusion U-Net pairs (image and geometry, each with reference and denoising networks) plus mesh reconstruction (ball-pivoting) at inference, which is relevant for practical adoption.

Limited discussion of failure cases or scenarios where the method underperforms (e.g., highly complex scenes, very large extrapolation, or thin/reflective structures where mesh reconstruction from sparse point clouds could fail).

Minor clarity/writing issues, including a non-standard/awkward term ('Instillation' for what is functionally an attention-map substitution/injection, not classic knowledge distillation) used inconsistently in places, and some grammatical slips throughout the text.

strengths: The core idea of cross-modal attention instillation—sharing attention maps between a deterministic geometry completion branch and a more ambiguous image inpainting branch—is a reasonably novel and intuitive mechanism for enforcing image-geometry alignment in generative NVS.

The pose-free, warping-and-inpainting formulation that extends to multiple unposed reference views and arbitrary target viewpoints (not restricted to a learned pose-embedding domain) is a useful generalization over prior single-image warping-and-inpainting and pose-conditioned diffusion NVS methods.

Proximity-based mesh conditioning (ball-pivoting mesh conversion plus depth/normal augmentation and normal-based masking) is a sensible, practically motivated solution to the noisy sparse point cloud problem common in off-the-shelf geometry predictors.

The paper provides a reasonably broad set of quantitative comparisons (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) against both feedforward (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat, LVSM) and warping-and-inpainting (LucidDreamer, GenWarp) baselines, plus ablations isolating each proposed component.
The multi-view aggregated attention design naturally generalizes to an arbitrary number of reference views at inference despite training with a fixed number, which is empirically demonstrated.
weaknesses: Table 5 (Depth prediction accuracy) is explicitly left incomplete ("Incomplete, under experiment being filled"), which should not appear in a submitted manuscript and raises concerns about overall rigor and submission readiness.

The claimed state-of-the-art performance is overstated: on RealEstate10K interpolative setting (Table 2), NoPoSplat clearly outperforms the proposed method on PSNR (25.03 vs 24.23) and SSIM (0.838 vs 0.820), yet the text claims "competitive interpolative performance" and the abstract/intro imply broad superiority; similarly in Table 1 interpolative 2-view setting the method only marginally or narrowly beats baselines, undermining the generality of the claims.

No comparison is made against the closely related pose-embedded generative multi-view diffusion methods explicitly discussed in Related Work (CAT3D, MVDream, SV3D, Gen3C, ReconFusion), despite these being natural and important baselines for extrapolative generative NVS; only feedforward reconstruction methods and simpler single-image warping-and-inpainting baselines are evaluated.

PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against a single ground truth are poor metrics for extrapolative, highly ambiguous hallucinated regions where multiple plausible completions exist; no perceptual/human study, FID-like distributional metric, or diversity analysis is provided to properly assess generative quality in extrapolation, which is the paper's central claimed strength.

Baseline numbers for LucidDreamer and GenWarp on DTU appear implausibly low (PSNR ~9-11), raising concerns about whether these baselines were correctly tuned/implemented for fair comparison, especially since the paper's own method uses the same VGGT geometry backbone as these baselines but achieves much higher scores.

The extrapolative view selection protocol (furthest cameras in DTU, latter/first third of frames in RealEstate10K) is defined entirely by the authors without clear justification of fairness or sensitivity to this choice, and could be tuned to favor the proposed method.

No discussion of computational cost, inference time, or training resource requirements for this comparatively heavy dual-UNet, dual-reference-network, multi-view aggregated-attention architecture, despite practical significance for reproducibility and deployment.

The appendix and several result sections are written with generic, repetitive, and vague boilerplate language (e.g., nearly identical figure captions and unsubstantiated superlative claims like "remarkable flexibility," "substantially improves," "critical insight") without corresponding quantitative support, which weakens confidence in the rigor of the reported analysis (e.g., pointmap normalization and single-view results are only qualitatively, not quantitatively, ablated).

No explicit limitations section or discussion of failure cases (e.g., thin/complex structures for ball-pivoting mesh reconstruction, scenes with highly inaccurate off-the-shelf geometry, or very large extrapolation where hallucination quality degrades).

Reproducibility is limited: project page link is blank, no mention of code release, and some implementation details (e.g., exact mesh conditioning hyperparameters, training schedule specifics such as a seemingly truncated learning rate "1×10") are incomplete or appear to contain typographical/formatting errors.

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated gap between feedforward (reconstructive, limited extrapolation) and generative pose-embedded NVS methods (limited to in-domain poses), proposing a pose-free warping-and-inpainting framework that works at arbitrary target viewpoints.

The cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI) idea is a reasonably novel and well-motivated mechanism: using the more deterministic geometry-completion attention maps to regularize image inpainting, while letting geometry benefit from semantic image features, supported by an intuitive visualization (Fig. 3) showing the mechanism's effect.

Joint generation of aligned RGB and pointmap/geometry avoids the scale-and-shift ambiguity that plagues standard monocular depth estimators, which is a genuine practical benefit over naive depth-prediction pipelines.

Reasonably thorough empirical validation across three datasets (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) and against a good set of relevant baselines (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat, DUSt3R, LucidDreamer, GenWarp, LVSM), with consistent gains in extrapolative settings and competitive performance in interpolative settings.

Component-wise ablations (pointmap conditioning, proximity-based mesh conditioning, cross-modal instillation) show monotonic improvement, supporting the claimed contributions, and additional analyses (number of input views, pointmap normalization) add useful insight into model behavior and generalization.
weaknesses: Table 5 (depth prediction accuracy) is explicitly left incomplete in the submitted manuscript ("Incomplete, under experiment being filled"), which is a significant issue for a submission under review — it suggests insufficient polish/finalization and raises doubts about whether other quantitative claims were fully vetted before submission.

The paper does not compare against other diffusion-based multi-view/pose-embedded generative baselines explicitly discussed in related work (e.g., CAT3D, MVDream, Gen3C, ReconFusion), despite positioning itself against this class of methods in the introduction; this weakens the completeness of the empirical comparison.

No analysis of computational cost/inference time/memory overhead of running two parallel U-Nets (image + geometry) with cross-modal attention instillation versus single-branch baselines, which is relevant given the added architectural complexity.

Quantitative evaluation relies on PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, which are known to be poor proxies for generative quality in genuinely ambiguous extrapolative regions (where many plausible hallucinations exist); no FID, user study, or perceptual study is included to substantiate 'high-fidelity' extrapolation claims beyond qualitative figures.

The extrapolative/interpolative view split heuristics (furthest cameras in DTU, convex-hull condition, forward-frame splits in RealEstate10K) are reasonable but somewhat ad hoc and not standardized against prior benchmarks, making it harder to compare these numbers to future work or verify they aren't cherry-picked splits favoring the proposed method.

Minor writing/clarity issues remain (e.g., garbled learning rate value '1×10', typographical errors such as 'vlaues', inconsistent figure/method naming such as DUSt3R vs NoPoSplat citation numbers in Fig. 6 captions), suggesting the paper could benefit from a more careful proofreading pass.

The method depends heavily on a specific off-the-shelf geometry predictor (VGGT) for both training supervision and inference-time conditioning; sensitivity of the pipeline’s performance to the choice/quality of this upstream model is not analyzed, raising questions about robustness/generalization if a weaker or different geometry prior is used.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated technical contribution: cross-modal attention instillation, where attention maps from the more robust geometry-completion branch are shared with (or in this specific implementation, key/query features from the image branch are shared with) the geometry branch, exploiting complementary strengths of image and geometry generation. The motivating analysis in Fig. 3 is convincing and clearly explains the design choice.

Formulating both novel-view image AND geometry synthesis as a joint warping-and-inpainting problem is a useful extension over prior single-modality warping-inpainting works (LucidDreamer, GenWarp), directly addressing the scale-shift misalignment issue between predicted and reference geometry.

Extensive empirical evaluation across many datasets (Co3D, DTU zero-shot, RealEstate10K in-domain, and further zero-shot generalization tests on CityScapes, MegaDepth, Navi) and against a wide range of baselines (feedforward pose-free/posed methods, warping-inpainting methods, and large diffusion/video-based NVS models such as ViewCrafter, ZeroNVS, LVSM).

Thorough ablation studies isolating the contribution of pointmap conditioning, proximity-based mesh conditioning, and cross-modal attention instillation, plus additional ablations on pointmap normalization and number of input viewpoints.
Robustness analyses to noise and sparsity in the external geometry predictor's output, supporting the claim that the framework is not overly reliant on high-quality off-the-shelf geometry.
Good practical advantages demonstrated, including pose-free operation, flexible number of reference views, and competitive inference time relative to alternative large-model NVS baselines.
weaknesses: Evaluating hallucinated/extrapolated content with pixel-wise metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) is questionable, since ground-truth comparison for regions unseen by the model is inherently ill-posed (many plausible completions exist); a perceptual user study or distribution-based metric (e.g., FID) would better validate claims of "high-fidelity extrapolative synthesis," but none is provided.

The training pipeline supervises against pseudo-ground-truth geometry generated by VGGT, and inference also relies on VGGT for correspondence conditioning; this creates a potential circularity/confound where the system may be implicitly tuned to VGGT's biases, complicating fair comparison with baselines that use different or no external geometry priors.

Several baseline comparisons may not be entirely apples-to-apples: e.g., PixelSplat/MVSplat are posed feedforward methods not designed for large extrapolation, and the paper's "fair comparison" protocol for geometry backbones is not fully detailed for all baselines.

No explicit discussion of failure cases or limitations of the proposed method (e.g., under very sparse/no meaningful reference overlap, or with more than mild inaccuracies in camera pose estimation from VGGT).
Missing quantitative (only qualitative) comparison against LucidDreamer/GenWarp on the Co3D dataset, despite providing this on DTU.

Results appear to be single-run without variance/confidence intervals, common in this subfield but limiting robustness of comparative claims, especially where PSNR gaps against some baselines are relatively small (e.g., RealEstate10K interpolative setting).

The overall technical contribution, while a sensible combination, leans on established building blocks (reference-network-based conditioning from AnimateAnyone, warping-and-inpainting from LucidDreamer/GenWarp, and Marigold-style geometry diffusion), so novelty is somewhat incremental beyond the cross-modal attention instillation idea itself.

No explicit discussion of how errors in camera pose estimation (as opposed to just noise/sparsity in points) would propagate through the pipeline, which is an important practical robustness question given the pose-free claim.

strengths: The paper tackles a well-motivated problem: achieving aligned image and geometry generation in a pose-free, warping-and-inpainting NVS framework, bridging the gap between feedforward (interpolative) methods and generative (extrapolative) methods.

The proposed cross-Modal Attention Instillation (MoAI) mechanism, which transplants attention maps from the image branch into the geometry branch, is a reasonably novel and intuitive idea motivated by a clear empirical observation (Fig. 3) that geometry completion is more deterministic/robust than image inpainting.

Extensive ablation studies (Table 3, Fig. 15, Fig. 8) and robustness analyses (Gaussian noise, masking sparsity, varying number of viewpoints, cross-predictor alignment with DepthAnything v3) substantiate the individual contributions of components and demonstrate some degree of robustness to imperfect off-the-shelf geometry.

The method shows strong zero-shot generalization across many datasets (DTU, Co3D, RealEstate10K, Navi, MegaDepth, CityScapes), and qualitative results look visually compelling with aligned geometry and image outputs.
Reasonable computational efficiency compared to optimization-heavy baselines (e.g., ZeroNVS, ViewCrafter), with inference times reported transparently in the appendix.
weaknesses: The quantitative gains over baselines, while present, are often modest in absolute terms (e.g., PSNR improvements of ~1-3 dB in several tables), and some baselines (e.g., MVSplat, PixelSplat on DTU) are evaluated zero-shot/out-of-domain, raising concerns about fairness of comparison since these methods were not designed/trained for such generalization while the proposed method may have broader or more suited training data/supervision (VGGT pseudo-GT).

The paper relies heavily on pseudo-ground-truth geometry from VGGT for both correspondence conditioning and as supervision targets (used in MSE loss for geometry completion). This creates a methodological concern: the model's geometry quality is fundamentally bounded by/entangled with a single external predictor's biases, and the 'alignment' claims may be partially an artifact of using the same source for condition and supervision, which is not critically discussed.

No explicit ground-truth 3D/mesh-based geometry evaluation metric is reported in the main tables (e.g., Chamfer distance against real scanned geometry) — the 'geometry' quantitative results in Table 4 and elsewhere use Abs.Rel and δ1.25 relative to VGGT-derived pseudo-GT rather than true sensor-based 3D ground truth (DTU provides real scans), undermining the strength of core claims about 'geometrically aligned' synthesis.

The architecture is quite complex (dual U-Net branches, reference networks, mesh conditioning, normal masking, camera-space normalization, multi-stage training), but the paper does not report total parameter count, training compute/cost, or wall-clock training time, limiting reproducibility and practical assessment of the method's cost-benefit tradeoff.

Several important ablations are missing or under-explored: e.g., no ablation isolating the effect of the geometry-to-image direction vs image-to-geometry direction of MoAI (is sharing bidirectional, or could sharing geometry attention into image also help, given the claimed complementary relationship?); no analysis of sensitivity to the specific off-the-shelf geometry predictor besides one appendix figure.

The writing in several places overclaims specific numerical comparisons (e.g., "+0.32dB PSNR... surpasses LVSM") that are marginal and within likely noise/variance across scenes, without reporting error bars, variance, or statistical significance over multiple runs/seeds.

The comparison protocol for extrapolative vs interpolative view definitions appears to be defined by the authors themselves (convex hull criterion) without clear validation that this matches standard community definitions, making cross-paper comparability uncertain.

Related work on recent pose-free/feedforward large reconstruction models is covered, but the discussion of concurrent or very recent works on similar warping+diffusion joint image-geometry synthesis is sparse, and the degree of genuine novelty versus combination of known techniques (Marigold, VGGT, aggregated attention from GenWarp, reference networks from Animate Anyone) could be more rigorously delineated.

strengths: The paper introduces a reasonably novel cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI) mechanism that shares attention maps between image and geometry diffusion branches, with a clear motivating analysis (Fig. 3) showing the complementary failure modes of each modality before fusion.

Extensive empirical evaluation across many datasets (Co3D, DTU zero-shot, RealEstate10K in-domain, Navi, CityScapes, MegaDepth) and against a wide range of baselines (feedforward splatting methods, warping-and-inpainting methods, and large model-based NVS methods like LVSM, ZeroNVS, ViewCrafter).

Strong extrapolative-view performance, which is a genuinely difficult and underexplored setting compared to interpolative NVS, with convincing qualitative examples of plausible hallucination beyond 90° viewpoint changes.

Thorough ablation studies isolating the contribution of pointmap conditioning, proximity-based mesh conditioning, and cross-modal attention instillation, plus robustness experiments to geometric noise/sparsity and generalization across varying numbers of input views.

Practical advantages over prior diffusion NVS approaches: pose-free operation, no need for per-scene NeRF/SDS optimization, and competitive inference time (9.67s) versus much slower alternatives (ViewCrafter 209s, ZeroNVS hours).
Good engineering details provided (camera-space pointmap normalization, separate branch pretraining) with ablations justifying these design choices in the appendix.
weaknesses: Some baseline comparisons appear questionable: GenWarp's reported PSNR (9.85/9.54) is implausibly low relative to its interpolative design purpose, raising concerns about whether baselines were properly tuned/re-implemented for fair comparison under the paper's identical-geometry-predictor protocol.

The method is not uniformly superior: on RealEstate10K interpolative setting, NoPoSplat still outperforms the proposed method on PSNR and SSIM (Table 2), so claims of general SOTA performance should be tempered to the extrapolative regime specifically.

The overall pipeline is quite complex (off-the-shelf VGGT/Marigold initialization, ball-pivoting mesh conversion, dual-branch U-Nets with multiple conditioning signals), which raises reproducibility concerns, especially since code/weights are only promised for future release rather than provided at submission.

Evaluation relies solely on PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS style pixel/perceptual metrics for a highly generative, multi-modal task where many plausible completions exist; no human preference study or FID-style distributional metric is included to better capture generative plausibility in heavily extrapolative regions.

Novelty is somewhat incremental: the core building blocks (reference-network-based conditioning akin to Hu et al. 2023, aggregated attention from GenWarp, pointmap-based correspondence from DUSt3R/VGGT) are adapted and combined rather than fundamentally new, with the main novel contribution concentrated in the attention-sharing mechanism.

The paper lacks an explicit limitations/failure-case discussion, which would be valuable given the method's reliance on the accuracy of off-the-shelf geometry predictors and mesh reconstruction quality in more complex, non-object-centric scenes.

Geometry quality metrics (Abs.Rel, δ1.25) are only reported in the viewpoint-count ablation (Table 4) rather than as a full comparison against other geometry-producing baselines (e.g., DUSt3R, VGGT, Marigold) across the main benchmarks, limiting assessment of the actual 3D geometry fidelity contribution.
